work_experience.description:
A campaign/bulk-messaging platform built for large enterprise clients with a high volume of end users.
Client-server application with a REST API; user authentication via Keycloak (OAuth2). Development and testing run inside a closed corporate network with no internet access: remote Linux machines, an internal Artifactory instead of public repositories, corporate certificates, and dedicated test environments.
API test automation: Java, JUnit 5, REST Assured, Gradle build (Kotlin DSL), Allure reporting. Built a base test class that obtains a Keycloak token and applies the AllureRestAssured filter, parses endpoint responses, and validates status codes and response bodies. Analyzed test failures and separated real application defects from environment issues (repository access rights, certificates, expired tokens).
Member of the project's AI adoption pilot group: learning and field-testing AI tools on real testing tasks, then rolling the working practices out to the team.
Key achievements
Set up the entire autotest infrastructure from scratch on a remote Linux machine inside the closed network in 3 days: Gradle wrapper pointed at the internal distribution, repositories switched to Artifactory, corporate certificates imported into the JVM truststore, API test framework, and the first green smoke test against the environment.
Wrote a step-by-step deployment guide for the QA team: 10 steps plus appendices explaining the typical errors. A tester can now set up their own working project alone, with no walkthrough from me and no access to anyone else's repository.
Automated Allure CLI provisioning with a dedicated Gradle task, because the standard download is blocked inside the network. Report generation now takes three commands.
Documented the network restrictions that everyone used to hit on their own: separate access rights per repository, two sets of credentials (one for libraries, one for the Gradle distribution), and certificate handling.
Tech stack: Java, JUnit 5, REST Assured, Gradle (Kotlin DSL), Allure, Keycloak, Artifactory, REST API, Linux, IntelliJ IDEA, Jira, Postman, SQL/PostgreSQL, Kibana, Git, Rancher, k6

work_experience.description:
Bit2Lend provides crypto-backed loans to individuals and businesses. Users pledge digital assets as collateral and receive financing on transparent and secure terms. After sign-up and collateral deposit, the application is reviewed quickly, and once approved the funds are transferred to the client's account. The platform is GDPR-compliant and uses multi-layer asset protection in partnership with Fireblocks.
The product is a high-load microservices application with a client-server architecture, integrated with Spanish banks, which keeps every financial operation compliant and reliable. We built systems for loan liquidation control, risk monitoring, and asset protection.
Responsibilities
Involved in every stage of development, from design through release and support (shift left, shift right). Functional, regression, integration, performance, security, and UX testing. Worked with internal and external integrations and feature toggles. Tested web applications and APIs (REST, SOAP) using Postman, Swagger, and DevTools. Analyzed logs in Jaeger and Kibana.
API/UI test automation
API: Java, TestNG, REST Assured
UI: Java, Selenium, Selenide, Allure
Built the autotest framework from scratch, wrote custom wrappers, and maintained the test framework. Set up parallel test execution (TestNG), Allure reporting, and CI/CD pipelines in Jenkins.
Worked with test documentation: checklists, test cases, bug reports (Jira), and test management (Allure). Optimized the regression suite, wrote test plans, and handled test analysis, test design, and task prioritization and distribution.
Worked with databases: PostgreSQL, DBeaver. Requirements testing (Jira, Confluence) and test environments (GitLab).
Monitoring and data visualization (Grafana). Worked with the Kafka message broker.
Onboarding, mentoring, and contributing to the growth of the testing practice.
Tech stack: Java, Selenium, Selenide, Kafka, Kubernetes, PostgreSQL, Jaeger, Grafana
